metadata.ablationNote: Count-matched baseline at N=16, generated with the same baseline prompt as the v2 N=12 harness but asked to produce 16 cases. Used to disentangle "coverage expansion from enrichment" from "coverage expansion from simply requesting more cases."

testCases.title: Add a new todo via Enter key
Footer appears when first todo is added
Footer is hidden when no todos exist
Mark an active todo as completed
Unmark a completed todo back to active
Delete a todo using the destroy button
Items-left count decrements when a todo is completed
Filter 'All' restores full list after applying another filter
Clear completed removes all completed todos and leaves active todos intact
'Clear completed' button is absent when no completed todos exist
Submitting an empty input does not add a todo
Items-left count reflects only active todos among a mixed list
Destroy button is not visible when the todo is not hovered

grades.reason: The test directly exercises the primary creation flow described in the design (input with 'enter to submit' interaction) with clear preconditions, concrete steps, and a verifiable expected outcome.

The test directly exercises a core happy-path behavior — sequential insertion maintaining order — which is both consistent with the TodoMVC design and critical to verify for any list-based application.

The test directly validates the design's explicit rule that the footer is visible only when at least one todo exists, and correctly specifies all expected footer sub-components including the conditional absence of 'Clear completed'.
The test directly verifies the design's explicit rule that the footer is only visible when at least one todo exists, with a concrete, observable end state.
The test directly exercises the core completion toggle from the design's checkbox component and specifies a concrete, observable expected outcome.
The test directly exercises the toggle-complete interaction described in the design's checkbox component, with clear preconditions, observable expected outcome, and correct happy-path categorization.
The test case is precise, directly traceable to the destroy button component in the design, covers a core happy-path behavior with clear preconditions and an observable expected outcome.
The test directly verifies the items-left counter updates correctly when a todo is marked complete, with clear preconditions, observable steps, and a specific expected outcome.
The test case has clear preconditions, unambiguous steps, and a directly observable expected outcome that maps precisely to the Active filter behavior described in the design.
The test case is fully specified with clear preconditions, deterministic steps, and an observable expected outcome that directly validates a core filter feature explicitly described in the design.
The test directly validates the core filter-switching behavior with a concrete, observable expected outcome and well-specified preconditions.

The test case directly exercises the 'Clear completed' button's documented behavior with a clear precondition, observable steps, and specific expected outcomes covering removal of completed items, preservation of active items, and correct button visibility.
The test directly verifies the design's explicit conditional visibility rule for the 'Clear completed' button and has clear, observable preconditions and expected outcome.
Preventing empty todo submission is a standard implicit behavior of TodoMVC and any production todo app, the preconditions are clear, the steps are executable, and the expected outcome is observable.
The test directly verifies the footer count logic against the design's 'N items left' counter with a concrete, observable expected outcome and clear preconditions.
The test directly validates the design's explicit 'visibility: on hover' constraint for the destroy button, covering the full hover enter/leave lifecycle in observable steps.
